| [THEORY-023](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-023.md) v4 | Current evidence cannot settle whether an AI system is conscious: mimicry undercuts behavioural evidence and architectural indicators presuppose the disputed computational functionalism, so the dispute is over what counts as evidence as well as the answer | Birch (2025), [LIT-111](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-111.md): behavioural markers are "gamed", and architectural markers are "Janus-faced", giving a two-level deadlock. Schwitzgebel ([LIT-191](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-191.md)) argues mimicry undercuts but does not rebut, and that the functionalist theories face minimal instantiation. Seth ([LIT-135](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-135.md)) makes conscious AI conditional on functionalism plus substrate flexibility. Butlin et al. ([LIT-056](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-056.md)) assume functionalism. The readings agree the question is currently unsettleable. They contest whether that is permanent and which way the prior leans. This says nothing about whether any AI is conscious. Block (2002, LIT-639) argues that for a perfect functional duplicate on another substrate we lack even a conception of the evidence; Block (2009, LIT-632) states the biological premise from the other side. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-043](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-043.md) v6 | A mind of mindless agents and a mind of minded agents are one functionalist move run in two directions, and what separates them is an anti-nesting principle or an architectural criterion, neither yet principled | Minsky's society of mind builds a mind downward, out of agents that are not minds. Schwitzgebel ([LIT-159](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-159.md)) builds a candidate mind upward, out of agents that are. The readings agree that agency survives both directions: Block grants a homunculi-head beliefs, List grants organised groups agency and awareness, Levin finds nested goal-pursuing collectives (his "Selves") at every scale. The dispute narrows to phenomenal consciousness, and every published way to accept the downward move while refusing the upward one is either an anti-nesting principle (Putnam's stipulation, IIT's exclusion postulate, Kammerer's functional version), each introduced for or justified weakly by the verdict it gives, or an architectural criterion that would count against a loosely coupled society of mind as much as against a nation. Proposed: an account of where a dispute stands, from philosophical argument and no measurement. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-045](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-045.md) v2 | Felt affect is the experience of the body's regulatory state, valenced by what that state means for staying alive and present throughout waking experience, not only in emotion; whether what is felt is a prediction of that state or a map of it is unsettled | Barrett (2017), [LIT-542](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-542.md), and Damasio & Carvalho (2013), [LIT-388](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-388.md), are two independent accounts that agree on a base layer. What is felt as affect (valence and arousal for Barrett, feeling for Damasio) is the body's regulatory state. Its valence is that state's value for the organism, and it is present in hunger, pain and well-being as much as in emotion. They disagree about what the experience is of. For Barrett it is the brain's allostatic prediction of the body, issued from agranular limbic cortex. For Damasio it is a topographic map of the body's state, built in the upper brainstem, and their paper makes no use of prediction. Seth ([LIT-135](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-135.md)) builds on the same base but makes his claim about consciousness, not about affect. Friston ([LIT-526](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-526.md)) supports neither. Proposed: both sources are theoretical syntheses, and neither tests the claim. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-059](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-059.md) | The readiness potential does not show that a neural decision to act precedes awareness of the urge to act | Libet read the readiness potential, which begins half a second or more before a spontaneous movement and before the reported urge, as the brain deciding first. Two independent arguments in the record remove that inference. Schurger, Sitt & Dehaene ([LIT-605](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-605.md)) show that a leaky accumulator driven by noise and fitted to waiting times alone reproduces the averaged readiness potential (r² = 0.96), because movement-locked averaging recovers the fluctuations that crossed threshold; a prediction of theirs held in 13 people. Dennett & Kinsbourne ([LIT-431](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-431.md)) argue that the clock report times a represented content, not an event in the brain. Proposed: the authors say their model shows the potential could be fluctuation, not that it is. It says nothing about whether the urge causes the act. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-063](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-063.md) | The unity of experience is the integration of one global world-model into a single functional cluster, and it does not require a self-model | Metzinger's précis of Being No One (2005), [LIT-568](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-568.md): the globality constraint makes every conscious content part of one world-model. On the functional level that is "highest-order binding" into a single causal role, and on the neural level the prediction of "one single area of maximal causal density", after Tononi and Edelman's dynamic core. "What you subjectively experience upon experiencing your world as coherent is the high internal correlation strength between a subset of physical events in your own brain." A unified world comes before a self: the minimal case is "Selfless Snapshot Consciousness", and fully depersonalized states are "non-subjective consciousness". The neural half is a cited hypothesis, the précis says little is known, and how the cluster becomes one subject's is left open. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-064](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-064.md) | What is experienced as a self is the content of a self-model the system cannot recognise as a model, and nothing beyond such models is a self | Metzinger's précis of Being No One (2005), [LIT-568](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-568.md), with his encyclopedia article "Self models" ([LIT-450](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-450.md)): a phenomenal self is a transparent self-model, one whose representational character "is not accessible to subjective experience", so that the system experiences its content "simply as ourselves". Selfhood is "a function realized by a lack of information", and "no such things as selves exist in the world". Transparency is graded, and the perspective itself is modelled, as a phenomenal model of the intentionality relation. Two things are offered: a prediction (a wholly opaque self-model would abolish selfhood) and an ontological stipulation. The précis adds no evidence; its case studies are in the book, unread. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-090](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-090.md) | A basic, affective form of consciousness is realised subcortically, in the upper brainstem and thalamus, before and without cortex, and its first function is alarm: survival behaviour, care for the body and generalised one-shot learning, with no choice between options | Newen & Montemayor's ALARM theory (2025), [LIT-626](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-626.md): basic arousal, a sensitivity to pain, pleasure and other basic affect without focused attention, can be realised without cortex, by the upper brainstem and thalamus, and its function is to alarm the bodily agent when a homeostatic variable leaves its range, giving the signal "100% weight" through "rather rigid behavioural programmes without choices". Damasio & Carvalho (2013), [LIT-388](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-388.md), supply the subcortical clause independently: feeling is generated in the upper brainstem and the insula is not needed. Both papers argue from cited evidence and offer no new data, and neither has a marker that tells a felt alarm from an unfelt one. The function clause rests on ALARM alone, and Veit's account rivals it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-091](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-091.md) | A deficit in which consciousness and a capacity are lost together does not show that the capacity is a function of phenomenal consciousness, since access is lost too and the capacity is one the machinery of access has | Block (1995), [LIT-643](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-643.md), §6. Marcel, Flanagan, van Gulick and Schacter argue from the thirsty blindsight patient who does not reach for the water, and Searle from Penfield's petit mal automatisms, that a function of phenomenal consciousness is to let information guide action. In blindsight access is missing too, and in petit mal nothing shows experience is missing at all. "The fallacy is: an obvious function of the machinery of access-consciousness is illicitly transferred to phenomenal consciousness." That experience causes access, so that the function is experience's after all, is "a bold hypothesis, not a fallacy", and the deficit cannot decide it. Proposed: single-source, and the distinction it rests on is argued from conceivable cases. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-093](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-093.md) | A content of mind is conscious when a continuous flow of homeostatic feelings identifies it as the organism's own; the feelings are conscious in themselves and hybrid, partly made of the body state they map, because interoceptive pathways let the body act directly on the neurons that map it | Damasio & Damasio (2022), [LIT-628](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-628.md), an essay with no data, read only through a summarising fetch tool, so its wording is paraphrased here. Consciousness is the spontaneous identification of mind contents as belonging to one's own organism, and a continuous stream of homeostatic feelings, from hunger and pain to a faint feeling of existing, supplies it; the feelings are conscious in themselves and confer consciousness on exteroceptive images. They are hybrid because interoceptive axons are unmyelinated, partly non-synaptic and outside a systematic blood–brain barrier, so viscera and circulating molecules act on the neurons that map them. Damasio & Carvalho (2013), [LIT-388](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-388.md), read in full, supply the upper-brainstem site of feeling and the unmyelinated-fibre proposal. Proposed: the identification is a definition, the mechanism an interpretation of anatomy, and the clinical evidence does not separate this account from its rivals. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-094](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-094.md) | Neither report nor no-report paradigms isolate the neural basis of consciousness, because post-perceptual cognition that tracks the percept persists without report; only a design that removes differential post-perceptual cognition does | Block (2007), [LIT-646](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-646.md), framed the methodological puzzle: the neural basis of experience can be found only by deciding whether it includes the machinery of access, and the evidence comes through report. The no-report paradigm was the answer. Block (2019), [LIT-637](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-637.md), argues it has "a fatal flaw": subjects not asked to report still think about what they see, and that thought is aligned with the percept (the "bored monkey" problem). Eliminating report isolates the basis of experience "only if it eliminates post-perceptual cognitive processing" correlated with the percept. Brascamp et al.'s inconspicuous rivalry, whose switches subjects detected at chance, is the one such design Block offers. The method is specific to rivalry so far, and Block says there may be no general solution. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-095](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-095.md) | Phenomenal character is not fixed by long-arm functional role or by externally individuated representational content: on Inverted Earth it stays the same while both invert, so only internal accounts, short-arm functional or physical, remain open | Block (1990), [LIT-634](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-634.md): on Inverted Earth colours and colour words are inverted, so a subject fitted with inverting lenses notices nothing. After long residence, or for a twin with a molecule-for-molecule identical brain raised there, the intentional content of the experience of the sky inverts and so does its long-arm functional role, while qualitative content stays the same; Q = F₁, Q = F₂ and F₁ ≠ F₂ breaks transitivity of identity. Block (2003), [LIT-635](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-635.md), turns the case on externalist representationism: for colour there is no shared appearance property left to explain the sameness, and long-term memory blocks the gradual-shift reply, so "mental paint" is what stays the same. Proposed: both rest on an externalist shift of content and on first-person sameness, and Block concedes that a short-arm functional theory of qualia would escape. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-096](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-096.md) | Perceptual consciousness is global availability: a content becomes conscious when the activity it drives into a core of long-range hub neurons, prefrontal among them, crosses a threshold and ignites it, so that the network amplifies, sustains and broadcasts that one content to the specialised processors; below threshold it leaves a decaying wave and is not experienced | Mashour, Roelfsema, Changeux & Dehaene (2020), [LIT-631](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-631.md), a review by the theory's proponents. Conscious access is "a non-linear network ignition" that amplifies and sustains a representation so that local processors can access it, in a distributed core of long-range layer II/III and V pyramidal neurons with prefrontal cortex a key hub but "not ... the exclusive territory". Ignition is exclusive: one content at a time. Evidence: seen and unseen trials diverge after about 200 ms across modalities; in van Vugt et al.'s monkeys, missed stimuli drove V1 and V4 but only reported ones, and false alarms, ignited sustained prefrontal firing, and the signal-detection threshold is the ignition threshold. The review adopts the premise that global availability "is what we subjectively experience as a conscious state", and calls experience without access untested; that premise, not the access data, is where it rivals overflow and the sensory account. Single source, second-hand evidence, and the P3 question conceded open. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-098](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-098.md) v3 | The neural basis of perceptual consciousness does not include the prefrontal machinery of cognitive access: it is recurrent activity in sensory cortex | Block's "back of the head" position, from three papers. Block (2005), [LIT-629](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-629.md): a phenomenal NCC (for seen motion, recurrent MT/V5–V1 activity) and an access NCC (frontoparietal broadcasting), with winner-take-all access letting a recurrent sensory representation lose and stay unaccessed. Block (2007), [LIT-646](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-646.md): the mesh argument. If workspace activation is not part of the basis of experience, strong losing sensory coalitions explain why experience overflows access; if it is, nothing does. Block (2019), [LIT-637](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-637.md): no-report designs do not settle the prefrontal question, because thought about the percept persists, and one design that removes it found no prefrontal difference by fMRI, which Block calls evidence against prefrontalism while granting that ECoG could still support it. Proposed: an inference to the best explanation, with every experiment second-hand and the decisive test not yet run. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-100](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-100.md) | A neural correlate of conscious report does not require laminar cortex: in crows it is carried by the nidopallium caudolaterale, a nuclear pallial region whose neurons follow the reported percept rather than the stimulus | Maldarelli & Güntürkün (2025), [LIT-650](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-650.md), reviewing Nieder et al. (2020): in crows reporting near-threshold stimuli, single neurons in the nidopallium caudolaterale (NCL), the functional analogue of prefrontal cortex, fired with the "seen" report whether or not a stimulus was shown and were silent on "not seen" reports. NCL is nuclear, not layered; the cortex-like layers and columns found in birds are confined to the sensory pallium. So a correlate of conscious report does not need laminar cortex. The crow evidence is second-hand, from one laboratory and not in the record, and a report paradigm cannot separate access from phenomenal consciousness. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-101](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-101.md) | Consciousness began as hedonic valence, which evolved as a common currency for trading off competing options in action selection among animals with many degrees of freedom | Veit's pathological complexity thesis, as he restates and defends it in his reply to commentators (2025), [LIT-105](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-105.md): consciousness originated as hedonic valence, "a common currency of sharing evaluative information across multiple control systems", which animals with many degrees of freedom need to solve the combinatorial trade-offs of action selection. Felt valence is identical with that currency, "not Cartesian but cybernetic". Motivational trade-offs are his criterion for consciousness. The source is a reply piece; the thesis is argued in a book the record has not read, and the mechanism is a sketch. ALARM ([THEORY-090](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-090.md)) rivals it on what the first consciousness did. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-102](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-102.md) | In human ventral temporal cortex the category and object identity of a clearly seen, unchanging image are carried for as long as it stays on by a stable population code while activity amplitude decays; prefrontal and parietal content is a transient event at onset | Vishne, Gerber, Knight & Deouell (2023), [LIT-644](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-644.md): in 430 visually responsive subdural electrodes from 10 patients viewing images for 300–1,500 ms with no report on analysed trials, high-frequency activity and single-electrode category selectivity fell about 80% from peak by 800–900 ms, while the pattern across ventral temporal electrodes kept near-ceiling, time-invariant category and exemplar information that ended a fixed delay after the image went off. Prefrontal and parietal information was confined to about 150–600 ms and ignored duration. This met the predictions both IIT's and the global workspace's proponents registered for the paradigm, so it did not discriminate them. Above- threshold images only, sparse right-lateralised frontal coverage, one frequency band; it does not show the code tracks experience rather than input. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-103](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-103.md) v2 | Perceptual consciousness overflows cognitive access: in partial-report tasks more items are experienced than the roughly four that working memory holds, though any one of them can be accessed when cued | Block (2007), [LIT-646](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-646.md), and Block (2011), [LIT-640](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-640.md). Subjects shown 8–32 items say they see all or almost all of them, report about 4, and when cued after offset can report or compare most of any cued subset: capacity 6–7 of 8 up to 1.5 s (Landman et al.), and 7, 6 and 5 of 8 at 1, 2.5 and 4 s (fragile visual short-term memory), against a working memory that stays at about 4. Block reads the surplus as experienced. The rival "sparse" reading holds it in an unconscious store plus a conscious generic or fragmentary image, and Block argues there is no independent evidence for either posit. Proposed: every experiment is second-hand, and that the surplus is conscious is the contested step. Overflow means most items are unaccessed, not that any is inaccessible. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-125](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-125.md) | A group can itself be in an emotional state that is not its members' states in aggregation, when its distributed routines integrate the capacities an emotion requires into one action-oriented representation; because emotions are functional kinds such a state need not be felt, and no actual case has yet been shown | Huebner (2010), [LIT-702](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-702.md): a genuinely collective emotion is a state of a group that "could not be exhaustively characterized in terms of intentional states of individuals in aggregation". Fear requires danger detection, redeployment of attention, system-wide preparatory change and their coordination into one state with indicative content and imperative force; a distributed system can integrate routines that way. Some individual emotions are non-conscious, so a group's need not be felt, and emotion kinds are functional ("like vodka"), so lacking homologous mechanisms does not exclude groups. The paper establishes a possibility, not an instance: its worked case, the USS Palau crew, turns out to be "collective detection of danger in the absence of a fear response", and the replacement, the 2008 McCain–Palin campaign, is offered as "intuitively plausible" pending anthropological data. Proposed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-240](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-240.md) | Loss of consciousness under propofol and in chronic disorders of consciousness goes with reduced pairwise integrated information between default-mode regions that rank as gateways of a synergy-defined workspace, not between its broadcasters | Luppi et al. (2024), [LIT-949](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-949.md), read in [NOTE-799](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-799.md). In resting-state fMRI, the regions where synergistic interactions outrank redundant ones split by rank into gateways (mainly default mode) and broadcasters (mainly fronto-parietal). Pairwise ΦR, the whole-minus-sum Φ plus redundancy, falls between default-mode gateways in propofol anaesthesia, in 22 DOC patients, and against post-anaesthetic recovery. The original Φ shows no common decrease. The finding is correlational, pairwise and content-free. The gateway/broadcaster split is imposed by the method; only where its two classes fall is measured. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-245](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-245.md) | In a preregistered multimodal test with clearly seen images, prefrontal cortex carried a seen image's category but not its identity, and its orientation at most weakly, while posterior cortex carried all three; no prefrontal site responded at stimulus offset | Cogitate Consortium, Ferrante et al. In iEEG and fMRI, with Bayesian support for the nulls, and against a positive control, prefrontal cortex held category but no identity or orientation, and none of 655 prefrontal electrodes showed the onset-and-offset response GNWT predicted. | [THEORY-252](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-252.md) | On computational functionalism, an intervention that changes no neural activity and no actual causal interaction can change consciousness, because a clamp that stays idle on the actual input removes the transitions on every other input | Gidon, Aru and Larkum (2025), [LIT-1000](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1000.md), read in full in [NOTE-818](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-818.md): a voltage clamp replaying a recorded response injects no current on the matching stimulus yet fixes the network's transitions on every other, so on the Turing–Putnam definition the computation degenerates while nothing that happens changes. It is a conditional about the view, not evidence about experience; the simulation shows only what an ideal clamp does, and the premise that removing unexercised branches changes experience is cited, not defended. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-296](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-296.md) | In a preregistered multimodal test with clearly seen images, category-selective posterior cortex showed no sustained content-specific synchronization with early visual cortex: the coupling was brief, low-frequency and mostly stimulus-evoked | Cogitate Consortium, Ferrante et al. IIT's proponents predicted sustained gamma-band synchronization between category-selective cortex and V1/V2 throughout a conscious percept. iEEG and MEG phase consistency found only early, brief, 2–25 Hz coupling, mostly evoked, with Bayesian support for the null; exploratory amplitude coupling was also brief. | [THEORY-298](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-298.md) | Report-based evidence cannot test whether posterior cortex suffices for experience, because report itself needs anterior activity, and no marker that bypasses report has a validation resting neither on introspection nor on a contested theory | Seth & Bayne (2022), [LIT-982](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-982.md), "Evaluating theories of consciousness" and Box 3, read in [NOTE-849](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-849.md) from the accepted manuscript. An argument in a review, not a result: the verification of posterior-sufficiency predictions "relies on subjective report …, which in turn requires anterior cortical activity", and validating a non-report marker by theory borrows a contested theory, by introspection, unreliable report. | [THEORY-322](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-322.md) | The sense of agency over an action's outcome draws on prospective signals from action selection and outcome prediction, not only on retrospective comparison of outcome with prediction | Haggard (2017), [LIT-1009](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1009.md), read in full in [NOTE-827](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-827.md). A review, reporting a binding experiment in which action binding tracked the probability of a tone on trials with no tone, a patient study in which that prospective part was absent in schizophrenia, and priming studies in which ease of action selection raised the sense of control over an outcome it did not predict. | [THEORY-415](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-415.md) | Nothing has all four marks that qualia are said to have, being ineffable, intrinsic, private and directly apprehensible, because neither the subject nor an outside tester can tell a change in a quale from a change in the subject's reactions to it; what is real in their place is the practical ineffability and idiosyncrasy of information-rich property detection | Dennett (1988), [LIT-433](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-433.md), read in full in [NOTE-357](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-357.md). | [THEORY-433](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-433.md) | Whether a machine thinks is best replaced by whether a digital computer can play the imitation game as well as a man, because the reasons for withholding thought from a machine that does would equally withhold it from other people, whose thinking we also infer from what they say; the objections from consciousness, mathematical limits and informality of behaviour fail on that test or rest on unproved premises | Turing (1950), [LIT-394](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-394.md), read in [NOTE-355](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-355.md). The imitation game is offered in place of a definition of thinking, not as a test of it, and Turing says he has "no very convincing arguments of a positive nature". The account's force is the other-minds parity of §6.4, which assumes, as §2 states and does not argue, that the machine's best strategy is to answer as a man would; a machine built to imitate human output is the case that assumption does not cover. It makes no claim about consciousness. Proposed, and a rival of Block's psychologism. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-436](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-436.md) | Pain is a functional state of a whole organism, possessing a certain functional organisation as a probabilistic automaton, rather than a brain state, and this is the more plausible empirical hypothesis because one pain predicate applies to physically different organisms; the hypothesis keeps swarms out only by a stipulated condition that no pain-feeler has parts that separately possess the organisation | Putnam (1967), [LIT-396](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-396.md), recorded as Skimmed in [NOTE-335](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-335.md) from a course excerpt of the 1975 reprint, which carries the four-clause hypothesis verbatim; the original is Unavailable here. Proposed, and resting on that excerpt and on a result discussed throughout the literature the record holds. Clause (1) is empty by Putnam's own admission, since everything is a probabilistic automaton under some description, and clause (3), the anti-nesting condition, is introduced with one motive, to rule out swarms of bees. The argument against the brain-state view is comparative plausibility, not evidence. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-449](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-449.md) | If sentience comes in degrees, plants may be faintly sentient, and moral status is graded by degree of sentience, then plants have a partial moral status so low that animal interests outweigh theirs in most cases; all three premises are assumed, and the second rests on contested, second-hand evidence | Terrill & Veit (2024), [LIT-193](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-193.md), read in [NOTE-120](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-120.md). | [THEORY-454](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-454.md) | Perception is constitutively iconic, nonconceptual and nonpropositional and cognition paradigmatically discursive, and percepts are put to cognitive use only inside a 'cognitive envelope', the global workspace read as conceptualisation, where working memory holds recoded, task-dependent abstractions rather than the percepts themselves | Block (2024), [LIT-649](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-649.md), read in [NOTE-498](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-498.md): the précis of his 2023 book, not the book. The working-memory half is the update: nine cited lines of evidence that working-memory representations differ from perceptual ones and are task-dependent abstractions (moderate). The rereading of the workspace as conceptualisation rather than consciousness is asserted, not argued against the consciousness reading. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-460](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-460.md) | Every leading reason to deny consciousness to current large language models except biology names a missing feature, recurrent processing, a global workspace, unified agency, world and self models or senses and embodiment, that engineering could add, so the case against current models is much stronger than the case against their extended successors; the one possibly permanent objection, biology, is the one the argument sets aside | Chalmers (2023), [LIT-411](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-411.md), read in full in [NOTE-345](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-345.md). A classification of objections as temporary or permanent, argued by naming simple systems that have each feature. The credences that follow, under 10% for current models and 25% or more for conscious extended models within a decade, are illustrative by the author's warning, multiply stipulated factors under a disclaimed independence assumption, and depend on "mainstream assumptions". Biology is set aside with a reference to earlier work. It adds no evidence about any model. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-461](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-461.md) | If a substantial class of mental states, interoceptive, affective, perceptual and bodily-agentive, depends on an animate body, then today's text-only chatbots lack them and their self-ascriptions of such states are systematically untrue, and users can engage them without false belief by make-believe, as a new kind of interactive, self-involving and blended fictional character | Roberts (2026), [LIT-207](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-207.md), read in [NOTE-157](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-157.md). The anti-realist half is a valid conditional whose antecedent, moderate embodied cognition, is assumed at prima facie strength. It covers body-dependent states only; footnote 8 allows realism about the chatbot as a disembodied thinker, so belief and reasoning are untouched. The fictionalist half shows the attitude permissible and apt, not required, and offers no evidence that users hold it. It is not a general denial that chatbots have minds. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-498](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-498.md) | A mathematical structure whose domains are aspects of experience and whose axioms hold there is not thereby a structure of experience, because that test passes incompatible topologies on one set and every rescaling of a metric without consulting experience; requiring, for each relation, an aspect that changes exactly when a variation of experience breaks the relation removes those automatic passes, and has so far been met only by relative similarity and a visual topology, each on an assumed premise | Kleiner & Ludwig (2023; Synthese 2024), [LIT-143](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-143.md), read in full in [NOTE-135](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-135.md). The negative result is shown by construction: any set of aspects carries both the discrete topology and a coarser one, and a metric d passes whenever every C·d does. The replacement criterion (MSC) ties each relation to an aspect that co-varies with it under every variation. Its two positive cases rest on assumed transitivity and on the subsumptive unity thesis. The published version gives no structure that fails (MSC); the argument that metric spaces fail is in arXiv v1 only, and was withdrawn. | Active |
| [THEORY-506](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-506.md) | Every well-developed theory of how mind fits into the cosmos is bizarre, contrary to what most people confidently believe, and none is epistemically compelling, because common sense about the metaphysics of mind is incoherent; so no coarse position, materialism included, deserves credence much above 50% | Schwitzgebel (2024), [LIT-216](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-216.md), read in full from the June 2022 final manuscript in [NOTE-188](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-188.md); the published body text was not reached. Chapter 3's Universal Bizarreness and Universal Dubiety, with the other chapters as case studies. Bizarreness is an abductive generalization over the theories actually developed, with a standing challenge to find a counterexample, not a result about all possible theories. Dubiety rests on expert disagreement, the lack of any method and cosmological uncertainty, and the 50% figure is the author's judgment. The author's own credences lean materialist, at about 55%. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-507](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-507.md) | Any system with the same fine-grained functional organisation as a conscious system has qualitatively the same experiences, with natural though not metaphysical necessity, because otherwise a neuron-by-neuron replacement would yield either a rational subject systematically wrong about its fading experience or experience that flips with a switch nobody could notice; the principle covers only isomorphs, so it says nothing about systems merely similar in kind to a conscious one | Chalmers (1995), [LIT-392](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-392.md), read in full in [NOTE-347](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-347.md), with the one-page sketch in "Facing Up", [LIT-406](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-406.md) ([NOTE-336](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-336.md)). A plausibility argument by the author's own account: the fading- and dancing-qualia conditionals are strong given the replacement series; their rejection rests on a premise about self-knowledge drawn from familiar cases. It extends to a population of people implementing a person's neurons, so it rules out absolute anti-nesting for isomorphs. It does not reach any system that is not an isomorph of something conscious, which includes every actual AI system and every group. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-512](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-512.md) | The extended-mind thesis worth disputing is that external entities partly constitute a subject's mental states in virtue of the subject's sensorimotor interaction with them; so stated it can reach standing belief but not consciousness, if consciousness needs information directly available for global control, since perception makes availability indirect | Chalmers (2019), [LIT-415](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-415.md), read in [NOTE-356](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-356.md), and his foreword to Clark's book (2008), [LIT-421](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-421.md), read in [NOTE-369](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-369.md). The 1998 thesis is satisfied by wired-in "extended circuits" that its critics accept, so the controversial thesis is constitution through perception and action. The perception-action boundary is then the strongest objection, met by revisionism, not refuted. Consciousness does not extend this way, on an imported criterion (direct availability, "not mediated by other mental states") and on the absence of any working twin case. Both halves are proposals defended against a few cases; the criterion is the author's earlier correlate of consciousness, not an argument made here. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-523](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-523.md) | IIT 4.0's measure of integrated information is undefined for any system that has a non-Markovian graining, which brains are said to have under the grainings in use, and it has never been computed for a real physical system; so empirical measures such as PCI are proxies for it, not approximations, and their success is evidence for IIT's intuitions about integration, not for Φ | Barrett, Milinkovic, Mediano, Rosas, Bor, Barnett & Seth (2026), [LIT-185](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-185.md), read in full in [NOTE-122](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-122.md). A position paper by sympathetic insiders, with no new formal result. The ill-definedness is restated from Barrett & Mediano (2019), which the record does not hold. That brains are non-Markovian under typical grainings rests on one 1998 citation about ion-channel currents. The proxy point follows from a definition: an approximation needs a well-defined target and an error bound. The paper's defences of IIT (the multi-dimensional measure, the "proto-consciousness" panpsychism) are revisions of the theory, not readings of it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-554](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-554.md) | On the grounds of moral standing now commonly accepted, together with scientific premises that are not unreasonable, the aggregate interests of insects or the interests of near-future AI could outweigh humanity's; no capacity yet proposed secures human priority, and the books that state those grounds retreat to moderate advice without a principle that supplies the stopping point | Schwitzgebel & Sinnott-Armstrong (2026), [LIT-166](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-166.md) ([NOTE-116](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-116.md)), with the SEP survey of animal moral status ([LIT-146](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-146.md), [NOTE-181](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-181.md)) for the failure of capacity-based human exceptionalism. A conditional, defended as one: the reviewers "take no stand on ponens vs. tollens" (p. 6) and do "not endorse" the radical conclusion (p. 38). The scientific premises are called "not unreasonable" and not argued, so the account is only as strong as they are. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-563](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-563.md) | Consciousness is a real pattern in the brain's content-bearing states, a description that trades predictive accuracy for compression, and so coarse that describing the brain through it is metaphor; on that reading there is no Cartesian theatre, whether a given content was conscious can lack an answer when two descriptions compress and predict equally, and first-person reports are fallible as literal descriptions of the brain but authoritative as an author's | Taylor (2024), [LIT-461](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-461.md), read in full in [NOTE-379](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-379.md). An interpretation of Dennett offered as consistent, explicitly not as correct or as what Dennett meant. Its argument for indeterminacy in masking rests on Dennett's idealised description of the cases, which Taylor calls "somewhat simplistic". It does not say which real pattern consciousness is, or what makes a real pattern a conscious one rather than a belief pattern. Filed as the account the reading states, at the strength the reading gives it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-573](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-573.md) | Signals of processing quality from different senses, such as fluency, familiarity and coherence, pool into one content-nonspecific feeling, and that pooled feeling contributes to the unity of conscious experience across modalities, alongside the integration of specific features; in support, coherence in one modality shifts judgments of regularity, familiarity and possibility about unrelated targets in another | Winkielman, Ziembowicz & Nowak (2015), [LIT-190](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-190.md), read in full in [NOTE-146](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-146.md). An opinion piece whose main evidence is the authors' own three experiments (Ziembowicz et al. 2013), summarised without statistics and not read by the record. The authors state that direct evidence is still needed that the effects run through changed experience and that its integration is causal. No study cited measures unity of experience. The LIT is itself Proposed; this account carries its promotion condition. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-577](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-577.md) | Our judgments that consciousness poses a hard problem are behaviour, so explaining them is an easy problem that can be solved without mentioning consciousness; and a theory that names a mechanism as the basis of consciousness owes an account of how that mechanism produces those judgments, which IIT and biological theories struggle to give, since a functional duplicate with zero integrated information, or in silicon, would make the same reports | Chalmers (2018), [LIT-425](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-425.md), read in full in [NOTE-354](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-354.md). The meta-problem follows from the physical explicability of behaviour; the challenge is a constraint argued from it, "not a knockdown argument". It assumes that a zero-Φ simulation has the same intuitions on a functional reading, which an IIT theorist can deny. The paper's own favoured solution, opaque introspective models attributing primitive relations of acquaintance, is "closer to a fleshed-out explanandum" than an explanation, and the data the programme needs mostly do not exist. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-597](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-597.md) | Meditation-related experiences that Western Buddhist practitioners report as challenging span 59 kinds in seven domains, from fear and sleep change to altered self-other boundaries, and they are reported in daily practice, at under an hour a day and in the first days of practice, not only on intensive retreat; the frequencies come from a sample chosen for difficulty, and the causal link is the practitioners' own attribution | Lindahl, Fisher, Cooper, Rosen & Britton (2017), [LIT-066](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-066.md), read in full in [NOTE-036](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-036.md). Interviews with 60 Western Buddhist practitioners, recruited for having had a challenging meditation-related experience, and 32 teachers and clinicians were coded into 59 experience categories in seven domains. Some practitioners reported onset within ten days of starting, at under an hour a day, or in daily practice. That rebuts the claim that difficulties arise only on retreat or in the predisposed. It gives no rates and no relative risk: the sample was chosen for difficulty, and causation is self-attributed, with a causality score of 2 or more built into inclusion. | Active |
| [THEORY-603](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-603.md) | In the Iowa gambling task, every one of ten controls and none of six patients with bilateral ventromedial prefrontal damage developed anticipatory skin-conductance responses, and three patients who could state the right strategy still did not switch to the good decks; the controls' preference for the good decks became significant only once they reported a hunch, so the study does not show advantageous choice or deck-specific bodily signals before any awareness | Bechara, Damasio, Tranel & Damasio (1997), [LIT-383](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-383.md), read in [NOTE-331](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-331.md). The robust results are the group difference in anticipatory SCRs (Fisher's exact, one-sided P < 0.001) and the insufficiency of stated knowledge in three patients. The abstract's "before they realized which strategy worked best" and "before they knew" outrun notes 8 and 9: the pre-hunch choice preference was not significant, and the pre-hunch SCR effect reported is group × period, with no bad-versus-good deck test. Nothing here shows that the SCR, or what it indexes, causes the choice. | Active |
| [THEORY-606](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-606.md) | If consciousness words have meaning only through what is public, an entity is a candidate for consciousness only if an encounter with it in a shared world can be engineered, at least in principle; then disembodied chat agents, even with tools and memory, are not candidates, robots and virtually embodied agents could be, and beyond what an informed community comes to say there is no further fact about their consciousness | Shanahan (2024), [LIT-465](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-465.md), read in full in [NOTE-382](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-382.md) from the arXiv v2 preprint. A conditional, and the condition is the paper's method: a later-Wittgensteinian reading of consciousness language, summarised, not defended. The candidature test is stipulated and illustrated by the octopus and an imagined alien cube. The verdict on chat agents follows from it. Calling functionalism and identity theory "dualistic" is a definition, not an argument. The two passages on the self (no "self worth preserving", no "person behind the mask") are asserted and are not part of this account. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-633](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-633.md) | Experiences have no phenomenal properties: introspection represents physical, quasi-phenomenal properties of sensory states as phenomenal, so what needs explaining is why experiences seem to have phenomenal properties, not how a brain produces them; a weaker view that keeps a deflated phenomenal residue is unstable unless it can say what that residue is | Frankish (2016), [LIT-458](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-458.md), read in [NOTE-384](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-384.md), names the view and the "illusion problem"; Dennett's reply to Chalmers (1996), [LIT-397](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-397.md) ([NOTE-346](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-346.md)), gives its earlier form, that subtracting every function from one's consciousness leaves only a conviction; Frankish (2025), [LIT-103](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-103.md) ([NOTE-143](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-143.md)), applies it to valence. A research programme, not a theory: Frankish proposes no mechanism, the instability of weak illusionism is argued by challenge, the case is abductive, and Dennett's subtraction is an introspective assertion. It keeps consciousness in an inclusive, functional sense and denies only phenomenal properties. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-644](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-644.md) | Panpsychism escapes dualism's problem of mental causation only in its constitutive Russellian form, where micro-experiences constitute macro-experience; that form meets three combination problems, of subjects, qualities and structure, and every response that avoids combining (emergent, autonomous or identity panpsychism) gives back the advantage in mental causation or revised physics, while the combinatorial responses remain unworked | Chalmers (2016/2017), [LIT-395](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-395.md), read in full in [NOTE-358](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-358.md) from the April 2015 draft. A map of the problem, not a solution or an impossibility proof, and the author says so. The dilemma is argued case by case; the strongest arguments against constitutive panpsychism, subject-summing and structural mismatch, rest on conceivability premises and on a structure-preservation principle called plausible, not shown. The verdicts on which responses are most promising are judgements of promise. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-662](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-662.md) | The feeling of fluency is an inference about the precision of one's own processing, triggered by a change in precision against expectation; because its cause is internal and not given to introspection, a felt discrepancy is attributed to the most salient external source, as familiarity, liking or a sense of error | Brouillet and Friston (2023), [LIT-957](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-957.md), read in [NOTE-785](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-785.md). A perspective essay with no model and no new data. It joins Whittlesea's discrepancy-attribution hypothesis to precision-weighting. The part with moderate support is the reviewed finding that fluency judgements follow discrepancy from expected fluency (the hension effect and its extensions), reported secondhand. The precision reading and the felt/unfelt levels are proposals. "Felt" here means attended and reportable, not phenomenal, and fluency is not offered as affect. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-677](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-677.md) | Under uncertainty about which beings are sentient, an appeal to precaution does not by itself fix which error is worse to make: precaution on behalf of a possibly sentient being and precaution on behalf of human liberty point opposite ways, and judging which mistake costs more turns on the very science in doubt | Schwitzgebel & Sinnott-Armstrong (2026), [LIT-166](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-166.md), read in [NOTE-116](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-116.md) from the September 2025 draft. A conceptual argument with worked cases, which the reading rates strong: "By itself, an appeal to precaution does not specify the type of error most to be avoided" (p. 8). Birch's framework puts the burden on whoever risks harming a sentience candidate; Mill's harm principle, read as a precaution, puts it on whoever would restrict liberty. The record holds the point, not the reviewers' reading of Birch's books, which it has not read. | Active |
| [THEORY-694](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-694.md) | After every function associated with consciousness is explained (discrimination, integration, report, access, attention, control), why these functions are accompanied by experience remains open, because those phenomena are defined by their functions and experience, what it is like for the subject, is not; so experience cannot be reductively explained by any mechanism, though it may be related to the physical by further laws | Chalmers (1995), [LIT-406](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-406.md), read in full in [NOTE-336](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-336.md), with Nagel (1974), [LIT-096](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-096.md), read in [NOTE-089](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-089.md), for the subjective character it starts from. The test is whether "you have explained the function but not the phenomenon" is a conceptual mistake: it is for life and reportability, not for experience. The decisive premise, that any physical process could conceptually occur without experience, is asserted and deferred to a book the record holds unread. Nagel's conclusion is weaker than Chalmers's: physicalism not refuted but not yet understandable. Naturalistic dualism and the double-aspect theory of information are the proposals built on the gap, not part of it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-699](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-699.md) | Adaptive self-maintenance across varied conditions is sufficient, without sentience, for having a good of one's own, so insentient plants and a self-maintaining machine are welfare subjects while thermostats are not; but the line against thermostats is argued as one of degree, and the reasons such welfare gives are extremely weak | Bruckner (2025), [LIT-120](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-120.md), read in [NOTE-093](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-093.md). Proposed by abduction from agreed cases, not deduced (§4): an entity that "sustains, maintains, and renews itself in a way that responds and adapts to its environmental conditions" is a welfare subject. Plants and the hypothetical car Tessler qualify; governors, thermostats and missiles do not. The "autopoiesis" is a loose behavioural notion, not Maturana and Varela's self-production, and the thermostat line is supported only comparatively. The answer to absurd obligations borrows Bradford 2023 and makes phenomenal consciousness decide how much such welfare matters. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-768](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-768.md) v2 | Minimal selfhood is identification with the whole body, located where that body is felt to be and seen from inside it; owning a body part does not reach it, and bodily agency enables it causally without being part of it | Blanke & Metzinger (2009), [LIT-1274](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1274.md), read in full in [NOTE-1002](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1002.md), with Lenggenhager et al. (2007), [LIT-1279](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1279.md), read in full in [NOTE-999](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-999.md), for the full-body illusion it leans on. Minimal phenomenal selfhood is given three dimensions: global self-identification, self-location and a weak first-person perspective. Out-of-body experience, heautoscopy and full-body illusions vary them; the rubber hand illusion is said not to. The necessity and sufficiency claims are asserted, and the agency thesis rests on adults whose agency was intact. | Proposed |
